Cloudflare (NET) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Over the past month, shares of this web security and content delivery company have returned 0%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -6.6% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which Cloudflare falls in, has lost 13.3%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Cloudflare is expected to post earnings of $0.42 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +50%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +60.5%.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $1.34 points to a change of +44.1% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed +40.5%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $1.86 indicates a change of +38.8% from what Cloudflare is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed +8.1%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Cloudflare.

News Provided by Market Updates

SAN JOSE, Calif., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Market Updates News Commentary - Cybersecurity stocks moved higher on Thursday. Palo Alto Networks reported fiscal first-quarter results after Wednesday's close and raised its annual forecast, and Reuters reported that the outlook lifted cybersecurity stocks as investors bet companies will spend big on defending against sophisticated AI-enabled digital attacks. The move came in a session where the major U.S. indexes spent the afternoon sharply lower as Anthropic PBC made its Nasdaq debut. With two more security names reporting in the first week of December, the group heads into month-end with fresh numbers on the board. Active Companies from around the markets with current developments this week include: Palo Alto Networks, Inc. (NASDAQ: PANW), Zscaler, Inc. (NASDAQ: ZS), SentinelOne, Inc. (NYSE: S), Okta, Inc. (NASDAQ: OKTA), Cloudflare, Inc. (NYSE: NET).

Market Updates Logo

Why the Sector Is Moving

Reuters described AI as reshaping the cyber arms race, helping attackers find and exploit vulnerabilities faster while increasing demand for software that can identify, block and respond to threats. The five companies below each report the business a little differently, through Next-Generation Security ARR, total ARR or remaining performance obligations, and their latest releases show where each one stands going into the next round of reports.

Palo Alto Networks, Inc. (NASDAQ: PANW) reported fiscal first-quarter 2027 results for the quarter ended October 31, 2026, with total revenue up 39% year over year to $3.44 billion and Next-Generation Security ARR up 66% to $9.73 billion. Remaining performance obligations grew 35% to $21.0 billion, and non-GAAP diluted EPS was $1.05, compared with $0.93 a year earlier.

For fiscal 2027, the company now expects Next-Generation Security ARR of $11.475 billion to $11.525 billion, total revenue of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $4.26 to $4.30. Palo Alto Networks also announced its intent to acquire Applied Compute, a platform for post-training and inference of open-weight AI models.

Zscaler, Inc. (NASDAQ: ZS) reaffirmed its first-quarter and full-year fiscal 2027 guidance at its 2026 Investor Day on October 6. For the first quarter, it expects revenue of $935 million to $939 million and non-GAAP net income per share of $1.15 to $1.16. For fiscal 2027, it expects ARR of $4.396 billion to $4.426 billion and revenue of $3.908 billion to $3.938 billion.

What Sent Cloudflare Stock Higher?

Image from Pixabay

Today's big story: Could Anthropic Stock Fall 25%?

Cloudflare (NET) stock rose 5.7% on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.2%. The company did not report earnings or file anything with regulators around the move. Most of its sub-industry, systems software, rose too. Of the 28 other companies in it with a market value of $2 billion or more, 23 gained that day. So what else was going on around Cloudflare that day?

What Was Happening Around Cloudflare On November 18?

Cloudflare's management spoke at an RBC Capital Markets investor conference that day. The chief financial officer said demand was broad across the company's sales, artificial intelligence and security businesses. He also told investors not to expect a repeat of the unusually large third-quarter beat.

The broader technology market had its own news. Technology stock futures rose before the opening bell after Nvidia's earnings report soothed worries about AI. The Nasdaq Composite then closed 0.4% higher.

Cloudflare derives part of its own growth from AI. Revenue for the quarter ended September 30, the third quarter of fiscal 2026, grew 39.2% from a year earlier. Management credited rapid growth in the Workers Developer Platform, a tool developers use to build software on its network. It also pointed to growing use of its network by AI agents.

Cloudflare Rose With Other Software Companies

Cloudflare's gain came during a broad rise across its sub-industry. The median company among those 28 gained 3.0%, meaning Cloudflare rose more than the typical member. Ten of those companies rose 5% or more.

Its peers rose even more. All five companies on Trefis's peer list for Cloudflare gained more than it. Fastly rose 12.6%, Palo Alto Networks 9.9%, Akamai 8.3%, Zscaler 6.8% and Fortinet 5.9%. The rise did not spread across all of technology, though. The sector fund XLK gained just 0.3%, and Microsoft, one of the five largest members of the sub-industry, rose 0.2%.

Where Does Cloudflare Stock Stand Now?

A one-day gain this large is common for Cloudflare. The stock had 23 rises at least this big in the prior 365 days, the latest a 9.3% gain on November 9. This one came after three straight losing sessions.

The stock returned 48.8% over the past 12 months, compared with 11.0% for the S&P 500. Yet the $300.91 close sits 16.6% below its highest close of the year, reached on October 9, 2026. Investors also pay far more for each dollar of Cloudflare's sales than they do for the broader market. The stock trades at 39.3 times its sales over the past 12 months, against 3.1 times for the S&P 500.

title: What Happens To Cloudflare Stock If Revenue Growth Slows?
detail:
What Happens To Cloudflare Stock If Revenue Growth Slows?
Trefis Team
Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:03 AM MST 3 min read
NET
^GSPC
AKAM
ZS
PANW
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Today's big story: Could Anthropic Stock Fall 25%?

Cloudflare (NET) stock costs 39.3 times its sales over the past twelve months, against 3.1 times for the S&P 500. The company returns no cash to holders, so that price is a bet on growth. On its November 5, 2026 call, management said variable revenue was the main source of the quarter's upside. Variable revenue is spending that rises when customers use up their prepaid commitments faster. So how close is Cloudflare to a slowdown in its revenue growth?

Cloudflare stock costs 39.3 times sales, yet holders get no dividend. If your savings have to pay the bills, the only cash this stake gives you comes from selling shares. The Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's, from 50 companies that have paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row. See what it pays.

Cloudflare's Growth Has Not Slowed Yet

So far, the reported results show no slowdown. Revenue grew 35.9% from a year earlier in the second quarter of fiscal 2026, followed by 39.2% in the third. Management said rapid growth in its Workers Developer Platform drove the third quarter in particular.

On November 5, the company also raised its full-year revenue forecast to $2,964 million at the midpoint, from $2,867 million in August. Yet the same forecast has the fourth quarter a touch slower, with growth of 38%. So management does expect growth to slow, though only slightly.

How Much Cloudflare Holders Pay For Growth

Cloudflare reported an operating loss of $223 million over the past twelve months. With a loss, a price-to-earnings ratio is not meaningful, so investors value the stock based on its sales. At the end of September, they paid more for each dollar of those sales than at 23 of the 28 earlier quarter-ends since September 2019.

That is where slower growth would show up first: in the price you pay for the stock. The stock has fallen hard before, even without a slowdown. In the 2022 inflation shock, from January to October 2022, Cloudflare stock fell 69% from its high to its low, while the S&P 500 fell 24%. Its revenue growth over the year to September 2022 was 51.9%, a little faster than the year before.

Cloudflare Holds More Cash Than Debt

A slower year would not leave Cloudflare short of money. At the end of September, the company held $5,129 million of cash and short-term investments, compared with $4,707 million of debt. It also generated more cash than it spent, recording free cash flow of $322 million over the past twelve months.

Palo Alto Soars 6% on Guidance Hike and $4.5 Billion AI Deal: "An Unprecedented Threat Environment" ©@jittawit21 from jittawit21 via Canva, @BlackJack3D from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Palo Alto Networks shares jumped 6% after revenue grew 39% and the company raised its full-year outlook.

CrowdStrike, Cloudflare, Fortinet and Okta rose with it.

Adjusted EPS grew just 13% as the share count rose 18% after stock-funded deals.

Demand looks strong, but per-share profit now has to catch up with revenue.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW:NASDAQ) is up 6% today after a record fiscal first quarter, a higher outlook and a $4.5 billion all-stock deal for AI startup Applied Compute.

The rest of cybersecurity came along: CrowdStrike (CRWD:NASDAQ) is up 6% and Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) is up 5%, and Fortinet (FTNT:NASDAQ) and Okta (OKTA:NASDAQ) rose too.

A big beat

Revenue rose 39% to $3.44 billion in the quarter to Oct. 31, beating the $3.31 billion consensus. CEO Nikesh Arora said customers "turn to us to protect them against an unprecedented threat environment."

Management raised its fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance to $4.26-$4.30 from $4.16-$4.19, above the $4.19 analysts expected going in:

Palo Alto Networks (PANW): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2028 (years to July) (TIKR)
Rivals get a lift

Fortinet, up 4%, gives the clearest read on firewalls. Its product revenue grew 37% in the quarter to Sept. 30, down from 52% the quarter before, and Palo Alto's product revenue also grew 37%, to $595 million. To me, that looks like spending lifting the whole group.

Okta, up 7%, is the test for identity, where Palo Alto now competes through CyberArk. Okta reports in early December, and current RPO growth above its 11%-12% guide would show that threat environment reaching identity too.

CrowdStrike and Cloudflare have no news of their own, so their moves are a bet that Palo Alto's demand is the group's.

TIKR tracks 55 analysts on Palo Alto Networks. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Palo Alto Networks, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Palo Alto Networks' Analyst Ratings

The catch is the share count

The 39% includes CyberArk and Chronosphere, deals Palo Alto paid for mostly in stock. Diluted shares rose 18% from a year ago to 837 million, so adjusted net income grew 33% while adjusted EPS grew 13%. Applied Compute adds more stock, though it's less than 2% of Palo Alto's market value.

After a nearly 30% slide from its highs, Palo Alto traded at 81x forward earnings at the last close. That's down from 101x in August but well above its five-year average of 57x:

Palo Alto Networks (PANW): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

(At today's price, it's even higher.)

The way I see it, a beat this size settles the demand question, but the stock needs per-share profit to grow much faster than 13%. The next test comes with fiscal second-quarter results, likely in mid-February. Management guides to revenue of $3.53-$3.55 billion, above the $3.42 billion analysts expected, on 837-842 million shares.

Today's big story: Could Anthropic Stock Fall 25%?

Zscaler (ZS) stock rose 6.8% on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.2%. The company released no announcement, earnings report or filing around the move. Instead, 23 of the 28 other systems software companies worth $2 billion or more rose during the same session. So what was going on in the market that day, and how is Zscaler tied to it?

Nvidia Eased AI Fears, And Zscaler Sells AI Security

On November 18, AI stocks rallied after Nvidia's outlook calmed fears about AI demand. The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.4% that day. Nvidia's own shares fell for a fifth straight session, though, because its much-awaited earnings call fell flat with investors.

Zscaler sells into that AI demand. During the company's fiscal Q4 2026 call on September 3, 2026, management said AI is quickly becoming the largest tailwind the company has ever seen. That demand covers its Zero Trust products, data security and security for AI. Bookings for security for AI rose more than 50% in fiscal Q4 2026 from the quarter before.

Did Zscaler Rise With Other Software Stocks?

Yes, and the stock rose more than most of them. The median company in its systems software sub-industry gained 3.0% that session. Out of the 28 other companies counted, 23 rose and 5 fell. Ten of those peers gained 5% or more, just as Zscaler did. The technology sector fund XLK rose 0.3%.

All five companies on Zscaler's Trefis peer list also posted gains, including Netskope at 12.7% and Palo Alto Networks at 9.9%. Zscaler moved with its group and beat the sub-industry's median, while three of those five peers rose more.

Where Does Zscaler Stock Stand Now?

A rise of this size is not rare for Zscaler. The stock recorded 13 sessions with a gain at least this large in the prior 365 days. Its last move this large went the other way: a 9.2% fall on November 5. This gain also arrived after five straight down sessions, ending with a 3.0% drop on November 17.

Over the past 12 months, counted from the November 17, 2025 close, Zscaler stock lost 32.9%, against an 11.0% gain for the S&P 500. It closed at $197.83 on November 18, well below its highest close of the past year, $293.11 on November 18, 2025. It also sits well above its low of $118.05, set on April 10, 2026. The path between those two points has been bumpy. Over six months the stock gained 13.4%, while the S&P 500 lost 0.9%. The past month, though, brought a 7.8% fall.

Zscaler trades at 9.6 times its sales over the past 12 months, against 3.1 for the S&P 500. The company is expected to report its fiscal first quarter of 2027 in December 2026. That report will show how fast its annual recurring revenue is growing, after a 25% rise from a year earlier in fiscal Q4 2026. Without the acquired Red Canary business, it rose 20%.
